message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it was right or wrong for me to delete my stepbrother's profile on my Nintendo Switch. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help her parents. I brought my Switch because my school is more than an hour away, and I wanted something to do during the train commute. My stepbrother really wanted to play on it, and it actually helped distract him while I studied. So, I made a new profile for him so he wouldn't mess up my saves. That seemed like a good idea at the time because it kept things organized and prevented any accidental deletions or changes to my games. When I got back to school, I started getting annoyed because every time I wanted to play a game or go to the eShop, I had to click on my profile. It was a minor inconvenience, but it annoyed me enough that I just deleted his profile. I didn't think much about it because I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit, so I figured he wouldn't notice or care. But then, this morning on the train to my dad's for Thanksgiving, my stepbrother picked up the Switch to play and realized his Zelda save was gone. He came into the kitchen where I was talking with my dad and started freaking out, even crying a little. Now he's shut himself in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because he knows my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn't think it was a big deal since I usually don't bring the Switch over when I visit. So, was it right or wrong for me to delete his profile? Let me think about the different aspects. First, ownership: The Switch is mine, so technically, I have the right to delete any profiles on it. But just because I can doesn't necessarily mean it's the right thing to do. I should consider how my actions affect others, especially someone I'm supposed to be taking care of. Second, the impact on my stepbrother: He was really upset when he found out his save was deleted. It's clear that playing on the Switch was important to him, and losing his progress made him feel hurt and upset. My dad noticed this and thinks it was mean, which suggests that emotionally, it was a negative action. Third, communication: I didn't talk to my stepbrother about my decision to delete his profile. If I had explained why I was doing it and maybe discussed other solutions, like setting up a better system to prevent accidental deletions, it might have been different. Instead, I just deleted it without any discussion, which could have made him feel disregarded. Fourth, the inconvenience: While it was annoying for me to switch profiles every time, it's a minor inconvenience compared to the emotional impact it had on my stepbrother. Maybe there were other ways to handle it, like setting up a password or using a different device for him to play on. Fifth, the bigger picture: Relationships are important, especially with family. Actions that seem small to one person can have a big impact on someone else. Building trust and showing consideration are important parts of maintaining good relationships. So, considering all these points, it seems like deleting his profile without discussing it was not the right thing to do. It caused unnecessary hurt and tension, and there were better ways to handle the inconvenience I was feeling.
